# UADE FORMATS -- which ones the demo system should support.
#
# HOW TO EDIT: change the first column to `drop` for every format you do not
# want. Leave `keep` on the ones you do. Nothing else needs changing; I read
# only the first column and the player name.
#
# What `keep` commits us to: that player's binary gets vendored into the repo
# and the format is expected to play on the Amiga. Players are small -- median
# ~4 KB -- so keeping a lot is cheap in repo terms. The real cost is that every
# kept format is one more thing that has to actually work on the device.
#
# Columns:  keep|drop   PlayerName   prefixes   size   notes
#
# Notes:
#   CANNOT WORK NATIVELY (speed_hack) -- only plays when an emulator may run the
#       CPU unbounded. No hardware equivalent, so these are pre-marked `drop`
#       and the build refuses them regardless of what this file says.
#   NO PLAYER BINARY -- eagleplayer.conf names it but the installed UADE has no
#       binary, so we cannot ship it even if you keep it.
#   already vendored -- committed and usable right now.
#   sample: <file> -- a module of this format exists in your DEViLBOX corpus,
#       so it can be tested immediately. No sample just means nothing to test
#       with yet; it is not a reason to drop it.
#
# eagleplayer.conf names 171 DISTINCT players on 179 lines (PTK-Prowiz owns
# nine of them, one per epopt type). ALL 171 ARE TRIAGED HERE as of
# 2026-09-23: 164 keep, 7 drop, none left unlisted.
#
# 164 keep | 143 have a module on this machine | 132 PROVEN on an emulated
# 68000 -- one real boot each, recorded in amiga/uade_sweep_results.68000.tsv.
# Of the 21 with nothing to boot, 2 have NO PLAYER BINARY at all and 19 have
# NO MODULE: not among the 17,358 corpus files (every one content-probed with
# `uade123 -g` on 2026-09-22; 2,875 resolved to a player) and not in Modland's
# 516,118-file index either, which was searched by prefix and by format
# directory on 2026-09-23. Each says so on its own row.
